Comment: Automated retrain pipeline: fetch real data -> train+evaluate -> promote or reject. Runs entirely on Lambda (no AWS Batch/VPC needed). Triggered either on a schedule (EventBridge Scheduler) or by a drift alarm (CloudWatch -> EventBridge). Replace every <...> placeholder with your actual ARNs before deploying.

FetchData.Comment: Runs fetch_data_handler.py: pulls fresh real data (SEC EDGAR by default) and writes it to S3, so TrainAndEvaluate reads current data rather than a stale or synthetic dataset.

TrainAndEvaluate.Comment: Retrains on the dataset FetchData just wrote to S3, evaluates the new candidate against the currently-deployed model on the same data, and writes the candidate to a non-live S3 key.

ShouldPromote.Comment: Only promote if the new model is a real improvement, not just noise -- 0.01 AUC margin is a starting point, tune to your data.

RegisterModel.Comment: Promotes the candidate: copies it to a versioned S3 key and updates the DynamoDB pointer that model_loader.py reads -- this is the only step that changes what the live inference Lambda serves, with zero redeploy of that Lambda.

Parameters.Subject: Distress model retrained and promoted
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('New model {} promoted. AUC improved by {}.', $.registration.version, $.evaluation.auc_improvement)

Parameters.Subject: Distress model retrain did not improve -- kept current model
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('Retrain finished but AUC change was {}, below the promotion threshold. Current model unchanged.', $.evaluation.auc_improvement)
